proposed_areas.title: Every credential stop is read as what it is and said once, in the person's time zone. This covers: Claude Code's refusal, usage limit and budget end (whether the Agent SDK ends the stream or throws); the subscription's share reached mid-run, as a stop under the policy; chat failures (no 'Answered with ...' note, one sentence per error); notifications about credential cards (one each, saying what the card says); chat's hold reply and start (they follow the Start dialog); a call cut off by Stop now (booked on its own credential); subscription task runs (they use the configured API address); and a waiting session queued behind another project (shown as next).

The money consent and the credential screens agree with what runs: one figure for the waiting work, which counts what the yes runs, and the yes runs only that work. Also: a task only the key can run says why it waits; the Start dialog under 'API key first' names the stop; the share and key-month stops, the one-off press and the UI's clocks say what is true now, in the person's zone; credential words follow design section 5. Plus 5 small items from other subsystems that may move: the merge press's head check, the onerepo fake daemon, project.create's tool description, the join refusal and the intake card's plurals.

proposed_areas.title: Chat answers from what was recorded and hears its own questions. It looks a record up before saying it is missing. A yes to a question chat asked reaches the model. The guard catches a change asked for in words. Recall lines say what the screens say: a session's failures, a card's question, a PR closed on GitHub, a joined project's lessons. The From line follows the records the reply rests on. A cancelled wait is never promised to go on. 'open <project>' opens it. No reply carries the app's marker, a tool name or glued paragraphs.

Thinking longer works on the real model and every line about it is true. Go ahead runs the answer it offered. The fast model's hand-over is never left to words: the app attaches its own ask, which spends nothing. The paid closer look is told what it is. Answer now never earns a new offer. The history is read from the prompt cache. A closed project takes no new work. The start, dependency, setting and old offer lines use the design's words.

owner_questions: L4-chat-309 (C3L-14): Chat reads back every change in a project whose failed task's card it sees in full, even 'add a task', which elsewhere acts at once with Undo. The reason is that the card's words come from a specialist or a web page. Should a card in which nothing is flagged as instructions keep that rule? Default until you answer: yes, every change in that project is read back first.

L4-chat-310 (LL-10): When you write to chat in German, should the app's own fixed chat lines ('Yes to what? ...', 'Nothing changed ...') be German too, or stay English like every other screen? Default until you answer: English, like the rest of the app.

proposed_areas.title: One repository, one project, said truly on GitHub and in the app. A removed project's take-over no longer counts, so the offer comes again. A take-over's docs pull request opens from the default branch, or the take-over says it did not. A Work-together project's Settings never promise a status pull request. A first plan keeps its decision record. Add to shows its drafting state, and the plan wait appears once. The take-over and host lines read well.

Merges and joined projects say what is true now. A pull request merged on GitHub that held a closed task's work says that work reached main. Merge cards close when their pull request closes. The Merge button reports a failed check at once. A merge already made on GitHub reads so. The join dialog, the status pull request, Costs, the header, Your files and Last result agree with GitHub. GitHub's slow answers are worded as such.

The 9 source keys of the "other" bundle went into 8 items. Every key appears in exactly one item; a script checked this against sources-other.json.

The one fix is L4-other-1 (minor). Sources: live4:L4-l3-4 and live4-step:l3:LC-L3.L3-research-3. I confirmed it at 4cf11fd:
- New task's who line has only two sources, runsOn and the web limitation (NewTaskDialog.tsx:176-178 and :369-378; model-settings-view.ts:185-193).
- Edit shows no who line at all (TaskDrawer.tsx:623 and :753-765).
- outcomeCriterion (verification.ts:65-70) gives every specialist the criterion "The work itself shows this outcome (a file, a page or an output, not only the report)". The brief (executor.ts:1126-1128) and the critic (loop/critic.ts:482-484) both use it.
- The reviewer's prompt says "You write no file". The reviewer is the only registry specialist with no write tool.
- So the app's own criterion contradicts the prompt. That makes it a fix, not model_only.

How the fix differs from the verdict's sketch: the line shows whenever a specialist that writes no file is chosen. A pattern over the typed words cannot reliably tell an output file ("review.md lists") from an input file ("found in notes/plan.md"). Naming the file from the typed words is on the cut line, and so is chat's read-back clause.

Proposed area l4-reviewer-report is small: 1 item in five parts. I suggest folding it into whichever area owns NewTaskDialog.tsx and TaskDrawer.tsx this round, or pairing it with an area that shares none of its files. Shared_files rules are in the file:
- loop/critic.ts belongs to l4-selftasks-check, and executor.ts to l4-cred-engine. This area changes only the outcomeCriterion call's arguments, one line in each.
- This area owns verification.ts' outcomeCriterion, New task's who note block and Edit's who select.

The other 7 items are not_a_problem, each with its reason:
- L3:LL-11. The snapshot refs refs/forerunner/before|first/<id> are internal lookup keys. Plain git log shows no id (L3-run-11 passed live). I checked with git 2.43: `git log --decorate` and `git log --all --decorate=full` do not show the refs; only `--clear-decorations` or `-c log.initialDecorationSet=all` do.
- L3:LL-12. The person-facing part, the filler "To fix" line, is fixed at views.ts:1527-1532 and passed live check 4. Asking the critic for an action would change critic.md and move the calibration baseline. If wanted, it belongs to l4-selftasks-check, which already edits critic.md this round.
- C6:C6L-20 is a process rule, not an app problem. The flock rule (one heavy command at a time under /tmp/frbench/heavy.lock) goes into every run L4 prompt; it is in this area's fix_scope. Two areas at a time can stand while every heavy command takes the lock: live check 4 ran two journeys that way for about 8.5 hours with no restart.
